question: The income of Raman is ₹60,500. He saves 26% of his income. If his income increases by 17% and expenditure increases by 50%, then his savings will:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let initial income be 100 units, making Savings = 26 units and Expenditure = 74 units.

New Income = 100 + 17% = 117 units.

New Expenditure = 74 + (50% of 74) = 111 units.

New Savings = 117 − 111 = 6 units.

Decrease in Savings = 26 − 6 = 20 units (20% of the original income) ⇒ 20% of ₹60,500 = ₹12,100.

**∴ The correct answer is decrease by ₹12,100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Initial Income = ₹60,500

⇒ Initial Savings = 26% of Income

⇒ Initial Expenditure = (100 − 26)% = 74% of Income

 Initial (Base 100x)
 
 Income = 100x
 
 
 Expenditure = 74x
 
 
 Sav = 26x

 Final (After changes)
 
 New Income = 117x (+17%)
 
 
 New Expenditure = 111x (+50%)
 
 
 

 New Sav = 6x

**Calculations:**

Let the Initial Income be represented as 100x.

⇒ Initial Savings = 26x

⇒ Initial Expenditure = 74x

After applying the given percentage changes:

⇒ New Income = 100x + 17% of 100x = 117x

⇒ New Expenditure = 74x + 50% of 74x = 74x + 37x = 111x

⇒ New Savings = New Income − New Expenditure = 117x − 111x = 6x

Calculating the overall decrease in Savings:

⇒ Decrease = Initial Savings − New Savings = 26x − 6x = 20x

⇒ Since 100x = ₹60,500, we find x = 605

⇒ Total Decrease in Savings = 20 × 605 = ₹12,100

**∴ The correct answer is decrease by ₹12,100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income & Expenditure Relation

The foundational equation is Income = Expenditure + Savings. Any absolute change in income perfectly matches the total sum of absolute changes in expenditure and savings.

Percentage Change Distribution

When applying successive or isolated percentage adjustments, always compute them strictly on their own initial values. For example, the 50% increase in expenditure acts purely on the initial expenditure ratio.

Weighted Average (Deviation) Method

You can also verify percentage balance directly by substituting values into the weighted distribution formula: Income × (Income % Change) = Expenditure × (Exp % Change) + Savings × (Sav % Change).
